newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau proposes bridge to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Macau proposes bridge to Hong Kong.

text.p: A senior Macau official on Thursday proposed a multi-billion dollar road bridge 37.9 km (23.6 miles) long to link the Portuguese enclave with Hong Kong, the Portuguese Lusa news agency said.
A delegation headed by official Leonel Miranda presented the HK$13 billion (US$1.67 billion) plan to their Chinese counterparts during a meeting in Beijing, the agency said.
"The response (of the Chinese side) was positive," it quoted Miranda, who is chief adviser to the Macau governor, as saying.

A Macau-based Chinese consortium would build the bridge across China's Pearl River Delta. It would be a private project and take about four years to complete, the news agency said but gave no details of construction or financing.
Property development sources in Macau said the project was conceived by local Chinese property developers.
At present most travellers between Hong Kong and Macau take an hour-long ferry trip.

Planning officials in the British colony of Hong Kong said they had not received any application for approval of the bridge, which appeared to rival a separate proposal from China's southern Zhuhai city.

Officials in Zhuhai, which borders Macau, said in January that preparatory work had already begun on a six-lane, 13.4 billion yuan ($1.6 billion) bridge to connect the city with Hong Kong, which returns to Chinese rule on July 1.
Macau reverts to China on December 20, 1999.

Zhuhai had applied for central government approval to build the 27 km (17 mile) bridge, which would have a series of spans connecting islands in the seas between the city and Hong Kong, the Xinhua news agency said in January.
